core_claim: Eventide SplitEQ 2 uses Structural Split to separate transient and tonal components so they can be shaped independently.
topic: How SplitEQ 2 separates the transient attack and tonal body of a sound, with six dynamic bands and source tuning options relevant to strings.
title: SplitEQ 2: Shape a Violin's Attack and Tone Separately
hook: What if you could shape a note's attack without changing its tonal body?
description: Eventide's SplitEQ 2 uses Structural Split to separate transient and tonal parts of a sound. Six dynamic bands can shape those layers independently, and new source options include strings, synths, horns and woodwinds. This is a music-production explainer with a symbolic violin example, not a claim of a live creator recording.
cover_payoff: Use a clearly symbolic sampled violin phrase to illustrate how separately shaping a note's transient attack and tonal body may change its perceived articulation. Do not present the sample or illustrated hands as a live performance recorded by Prince.
narration_script: Why separate a note's attack from its body? SplitEQ 2 separates transient and tonal components. Six dynamic bands can shape those layers independently. New sources now include strings, synths, horns and woodwinds on SplitEQ 2.

narration_evidence.quote: a six-band dynamic EQ that separates the transient and tonal parts of a sound, enabling independent shaping of each.
Transient and tonal content may be compressed or expanded independently with six dynamic bands

Eventide has also added seven new processing profiles for different types of material, for working with distorted guitars, synth leads, strings, synth pads, woodwinds, solo horn instruments, and horn sections

sources.title: Eventide SplitEQ 2: A True Pro-Q Competitor?
